notes: The part list is the same as step 1. Only the labels of wire1-4, wire7-10 and wire15-16 were made more specific to match the connections.

The chip sits across the breadboard centre gap with pin 1 at column 5, bank b, row f. Pins 1-14 are in columns 5-18 of bank b, and pins 28-15 are in columns 5-18 of bank t. Exact columns are my choice, because the pictures give only the approximate layout.
ATmega328P pin use: 1 RESET, 2 RXD, 3 TXD, 7 VCC, 8 GND, 9 XTAL1, 10 XTAL2, 17 MOSI, 18 MISO, 19 SCK, 20 AVCC, 22 GND. Pin 21 (AREF) is left unconnected.
Bootloader burning (ArduinoISP): Uno pin 10 to RESET, 11 to MOSI, 12 to MISO, 13 to SCK, plus 5V and GND. Wires 1-4 are removed after burning, as the text says.

Uploading: the Arduino's own microcontroller is removed. Uno pin 0 (RX) goes to ATmega pin 2 and Uno pin 1 (TX) to ATmega pin 3. These are straight, not crossed, because the removed chip leaves pins 0 and 1 connected to the USB-serial chip. The Uno RESET goes to ATmega pin 1. The pictures show these wires only roughly, so this follows the standard Arduino arrangement.

The 10k resistor pulls RESET (pin 1) up to 5V on the bottom + rail. The crystal sits between pins 9 and 10 via the two blue wires. Each 22 pF capacitor goes from a crystal leg to ground (bottom - rail).

Top rails are fed from the Uno 5V and GND and linked to the bottom rails by wires 11 and 12. Wires 9 and 10 take VCC and GND to pins 7 and 8 from the bottom rails. Wires 7 and 8 take AVCC and GND to pins 20 and 22 from the top rails.
The minimal no-crystal circuit is only described as an option, so it is not built. The crystal, capacitors and resistor are used, as in the main diagrams.
